name: box
description: Browse, search and organize Box files and folders with a short-lived access token
long_description: Bring a Box access token, such as a developer token from the Box Developer Console; the gateway keeps it off your Sprite. Saving, replacing or testing the token reads the token's Box user (GET /2.0/users/me) and nothing else. A Sprite can then list folders, search, read file and folder details, create folders, rename, move, copy, trash and restore files and folders, change their sharing and access settings, read and write comments, and manage web links, all as the token's user. Box access tokens expire 60 minutes after they are issued and Box has no long-lived user API key: OAuth, JWT and Client Credentials token exchange and refresh are not forwarded, so you replace the token by hand when it expires. The upload and download endpoints are not forwarded: uploads go to upload.box.com and downloads redirect to dl.boxcloud.com, which are different hosts. That is a limit on what this connector carries, not a guarantee that a Sprite cannot reach file contents: file details can include download links, preview links with their own Box-issued token, shared links and metadata values, and those work outside the connector. Users, groups, collaboration invites, permanent deletion from the trash, the metadata, task, webhook and event endpoints, Box AI, Box Sign and admin APIs are not forwarded either.

examples.title: List the root folder (folder 0); use any folder ID in its place
notes: Entries are files, folders and web links; use an entry's id with /2.0/files/, /2.0/folders/ or /2.0/web_links/.

examples.title: Search file names and contents
notes: Box limits search to 60 requests per minute per user.

examples.title: Create a folder in the root folder (changes your Box account)
notes: Box answers 409 when an item with that name already exists in the parent folder.

examples.title: Comment on a file; replace FILE_ID in the body (changes your Box account)

messages.401: Box rejected the access token. Box tokens expire 60 minutes after they are issued; generate a new one and replace the saved token
messages.403: Box refused the request (%{status}); the token's user or the app's scopes do not allow it
messages.404: Not found in Box, or the token's user cannot see it
messages.409: Box reported a conflict; an item with that name may already exist in the folder
messages.429: Box rate limit reached; wait for the retry-after interval and try again
messages.invalid_api_key: Box rejected the access token. Box tokens expire 60 minutes after they are issued; generate a new one and try again
messages.provider_unreachable: Could not reach Box; retry later

presentation.tagline: Browse and organize your Box files from a Sprite without putting the token on it.
presentation.setup: In the Box Developer Console (app.box.com/developers/console), open or create a Platform App, open its Configuration tab and select Generate Developer Token, then paste the token here. The token acts as the Box user who generated it and stops working 60 minutes later; generate a new one and replace the saved token to continue.

notices.title: Billing
notices.body: Box has no per-request charge, but Box Business plans include a monthly per-enterprise allocation of API calls and every request through this connector counts toward it, including the one `GET /2.0/users/me` sent when you save or test a token. Box limits each user to about 1,000 API requests per minute and 60 searches per minute and answers 429 with a `retry-after` header when exceeded.

notices.title: Scope
notices.body: Forwards the token's user (`GET /2.0/users/me`); folders (create, read, update, trash, restore, copy, list items and collaborators); files (read details, update, trash, restore, copy, list versions, comments and collaborators); comments; search; recent items; collections; web links; and the trash listing. The file upload and download endpoints, token exchange and refresh, users and groups, collaboration invites, permanent deletion from the trash, the metadata, task, webhook and event endpoints, Box AI, Box Sign and admin APIs are not forwarded. Routes are matched by method and path only. Query parameters and request bodies are not restricted, and the connector does not narrow what the token may do: a forwarded route can use every right Box gives the token's user, including enterprise-wide search (`scope=enterprise_content`) where Box has enabled it for that user.

notices.title: Tokens expire after 60 minutes
notices.body: Box access tokens and developer tokens last 60 minutes and this connector cannot refresh them. When a token expires every request returns 401 until you save a new one. Box describes developer tokens as meant for development and testing, and revoking one in the Developer Console deletes the webhooks that app created.

notices.title: File contents are not isolated
notices.body: The upload and download endpoints are not forwarded: Box uploads go to `upload.box.com`, `GET /2.0/files/:id/content` answers with a redirect to `dl.boxcloud.com`, and a connector reaches one host, `api.box.com`. This does not keep file contents away from a Sprite. With the `fields` parameter, `GET /2.0/files/:id` can return a `download_url`, an `expiring_embed_link` (a preview URL with its own restricted Box access token), shared links and metadata values. A Sprite that can reach Box's other hosts may be able to use them to open or download the file, with the access Box gives the token's user. Box issues the links and the preview token in the response; they are separate from the token you saved.

notices.title: Writes are real and can change access
notices.body: Updates, moves, copies and comments take effect in your Box account as the token's user. `DELETE` moves an item to the trash or deletes it permanently, depending on your enterprise's settings. Request bodies are not restricted, so an update (`PUT`) can do everything Box allows on that route, not only rename and move. On a file, folder or web link it can create, change or remove a shared link, including a public (`open`) link and its password. On a file it can also set who may download it (`permissions.can_download`, which overrides collaborators' roles), lock it, and set a retention date (`disposition_at`) that Box does not let you shorten afterwards. On a folder it can also let collaborators who are not the owner invite others or see other collaborators, apply or lift the restriction of new invites to your enterprise, and turn on an upload email address, which can be set to accept files from any sender. Creating a folder can turn on its upload email address too.

usage_notes: IDs in paths are numeric; the root folder is `0`. Paths with any other ID segment are refused.
Use the `fields` query parameter to ask for only the fields you need, and `limit` with `marker` or `offset` to page through lists.
Rename with `PUT /2.0/files/:id` and `{"name": ...}`; move with `{"parent": {"id": ...}}`. Restore a trashed item with `POST` to the same path.
`DELETE /2.0/folders/:id` refuses a folder that is not empty unless you add `?recursive=true`.
Request headers such as `as-user`, `boxapi`, `if-match` and `x-rep-hints` are not forwarded.
